title: Moving day
topic: A friend estimates when movers carrying a sofa up the stairs will reach the 8th floor
blurb: A friend is timing movers carrying a sofa up the stairs.
prompt: A friend just sent this in the group chat. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or let it pass.

segments.label: The break
segments.text: Freight elevator died mid-move, so the movers are hauling the sofa up the stairs to my place on the 10th floor.

segments.label: Check-in
segments.text: They left the lobby on floor 1 at 2:00 and just texted from the 4th floor at 2:06 — steady pace, no stops.

segments.label: The ETA
segments.text: Six minutes for four floors is a minute and a half per floor, so six more floors puts them at my door at 2:15.

segments.label: The prep
segments.text: I'll clear the hallway and prop the door around 2:14.

conclusion: 6 minutes for 4 floors is 1.5 minutes per floor, so 6 more floors to the 10th takes 9 minutes (2:15).

flaws.original: Floor 1 to floor 4 is 3 flights of stairs (2 minutes a flight), so 6 more flights to floor 10 takes 12 minutes — 2:18, not 2:15.
flaws.corrupted: Six minutes for four floors is a minute and a half per floor, so six more floors puts them at my door at 2:15.

diagnosis_choices.label: Floor 1 to 4 is only 3 flights (2 min each), so 6 more flights to 10 takes 12 min — 2:18, not 2:15.
4th to 10th includes both landings (7 floors at 1.5 min each), so they won't arrive until 2:16:30.
Six more floors at 1.5 minutes each is 10 minutes, not 9, putting them at your door at 2:16.
Carrying a sofa slows down after floor 4, so extrapolating the 1.5 min/floor pace misses fatigue.

fix_choices.label: Count flights climbed: 3 flights took 6 min (2 min each), so 6 more flights take 12 min (2:18).
Count 7 floors inclusive from 4th to 10th at 1.5 min each and expect them around 2:17.
Fix 6 × 1.5 to 10 minutes so the arrival time moves from 2:15 to 2:16.
Add a 3-minute breather on floor 7 on top of the 9 minutes so they arrive at 2:18.

flaws.explanation: Floor 1 to floor 4 is 3 flights of stairs, not 4 — that's 2 minutes a flight. Six more flights to the 10th floor takes 12 minutes, so they'll hit your door at 2:18, not 2:15.
flaws.why_tempting: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 and 6 × 1.5 = 9 are both spotless arithmetic. It glides right past that you start on floor 1 without climbing a flight.
flaws.catch_rule: When climbing between numbered floors, subtract the floor numbers to count actual flights — never take a ratio of the floor numbers.
flaws.hint: When you walk from floor 1 to floor 4, how many flights of stairs do you actually climb?

practice.problem: A runner climbs from the 1st floor to the 5th floor in 40 seconds at a steady pace. How long to climb from the 1st floor to the 9th?
practice.answer: 80 seconds — 1st to 5th is 4 flights (10s each), and 1st to 9th is 8 flights.

diagnosis: A 10th-floor apartment only has 9 flights from street level, so calling it 10 floors overcounts by one.
If the freight elevator died mid-move, the movers were already partway up before switching to stairs.
A sofa takes two movers, so you can't treat their stair pace as a fixed per-floor rate.
Most buildings skip floor 13, not floor 10, so 10th floor is actually 10 flights from the garage.
fix: Check whether they started in the basement garage instead of the 1st-floor lobby.
Verify if the building numbers the lobby as ground floor 0 instead of floor 1.
Count 9 total flights up front before timing them from floor 1.
Ask the building super when the freight elevator restarts before timing stairs.

diagnosis: Texting from the 4th floor means they paused to type, so the 6 minutes already includes a break.
2:00 to 2:06 is 6 minutes, which is too short a window to predict a 10-floor climb accurately.
Leaving from floor 1 and hitting floor 4 in 6 minutes means 2 minutes per floor, not 1.5 — wait, 4 − 1 is 3.
Starting at 2:00 exact is almost certainly rounded, which skews the 1.5-minute pace.
fix: Wait for a second text from floor 6 before estimating when they'll reach floor 10.
Subtract 30 seconds for texting time before computing their pace per flight.
Check the exact minute they left the lobby instead of rounding to 2:00.
Ask the movers how many rest stops they plan between floor 4 and floor 10.

diagnosis: Propping the door at 2:14 leaves it open only 1 minute if they hit 2:15 — too tight to clear the hall.
You'll be holding the door open 4 minutes early since they won't actually reach floor 10 until 2:18.
Propping a hallway fire door open before movers arrive violates building rules either way.
They'll actually arrive at 2:12 (only 6 more minutes), so 2:14 is two minutes too late.
fix: Wait until 2:17 to prop the door, since they won't reach the 10th floor until 2:18.
Clear the hallway now and wait for their text from the 9th floor before opening.
Prop the door at 2:11 in case they reach floor 10 in 6 minutes.
Go down a flight around 2:15 to guide the sofa around the last corner.
